title: What does CredentialDelete do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of CredentialDelete and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, CredentialDelete removes a credential under the issuer, subject or expiration permissions in the reference. [1]

Deletion revokes the credential's current ledger presence without erasing transaction history. Applications must check current acceptance and expiry rather than rely on an old screenshot. Match issuer, subject and credential type. Removing an attestation is distinct from freezing money, reclaiming a token balance or deleting the subject's account. [1]

The CredentialDelete reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using CredentialDelete, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
